label: The keyed trigger-index lane cannot be flooded by one large document: lookup() accumulates into a byPath Map keyed on document path, keeps one row per document scored by its best phrase, then slices to --limit (default 20) and sets truncated. Real query 'trigger index lookup' returned 9 results, 9 unique paths, truncated false. A per-file cap is a no-op on this lane.

The free-text lane floods only for some query shapes. Real ranker over one packet research/ folder (34 files, 594 matches for 'deep research'): 'deep research' -> top-20 over 15 files, max 2 per file; 'research' -> 16566 rows, top-20 over 8 files, max 12 per file; 'iteration' -> 10078 rows, top-20 over 6 files, max 14 per file; 'research iteration' -> 94 rows, max 6 per file. Single-token probes put 60-70 percent of a k=20 budget into one file.

The flood mechanism is the rank tuple, not file size: rankMatches sorts by evidence field, then match class, then path, then line. Match class is per-line, so multi-token prose queries scatter classes across files and stay diverse; a single token makes nearly every line one class, after which the path tie-break groups a file's lines contiguously and a k cut takes that block first.

At corpus scale the flood and the row count are an order of magnitude worse: the Section 2.3 count recipe over specs and .skilled reports 13113 matching files and 111342 matches for 'research', with one iteration log holding 3142 of them; 'deep research' gives 1588 files with a maximum of 33 per file.

Skilled already contains a fetch-side per-file cap in one of two recipe builders for the same lane: structuredCappedRecipe passes --max-count 1 justified as 'the second match in a file never changes that', while the wrapper that actually serves the structured recipe has no --max-count and ranks the full output. The capped builder's rationale is also wrong on its own terms: the second match is the only evidence the file has more than one, so it changes hit density and the elision count.

sweet-search solves the flood with three coupled parts, not one cap: applyGrepFileDiversity keeps perFileCap per file and maxFiles files while returning hiddenFileCount, hiddenMatchCount and hiddenSample; allocateGrepLinesWithFirstLine gives every kept file one line in weight order before any file gets a second, with weight sqrt(hits) x prior so source outranks test outranks generated; and elision is never silent, with an inline '(+N more in this file)' on each truncated file's last shown line and a tail '# +N more file(s) with M match(es) - e.g. ...; narrow the regex, raise -k, or drill in with --in <file>'.

The totals pass the elision line needs already exists and is exact: the count recipe returned 594 matches across 34 files for 'deep research' in the same folder where the structured recipe returned 594 ranked rows across 34 files. Today the rank tuple carries no per-file 'more' and no hidden-files field, so that count is discarded.

A per-file cap alone is not the fix: capping at one line per file still yields 13113 rows corpus-wide for 'research', so a k cut is still required, and a k cut without the guarantee pass re-introduces path-order bias by taking one line each from the alphabetically first k files. The unit is cap plus final-k plus elision line.

VERDICT Q2: ADAPT. Adopt the elision line (per-file '(N more)' plus a hidden-files tail) and the one-line-per-file guarantee ahead of the k cut. Adapt rather than copy: do not import Sainte-Lague allocation or sqrt(hits) x prior weighting beside Skilled's evidence-field/match-class tuple, which is a better relevance signal and would become a second ranker. Drop any cap on the keyed lane and the '--max-count 1' rationale as written. Build target: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/rg-wrapper.mjs (capped fetch plus totals pass plus more/hidden fields), reusing lib/rg-lane.mjs, with retrieval-conventions.md sections 2.1 and 5 updated. Size: about 80-140 lines of code, about 20 lines of doc, plus tests in runtime/cli/tests/rg-wrapper-recipes.vitest.ts. No new module, no dependency, no index, no daemon.
Two recipe builders for one lane disagree on --max-count; the uncapped one is what search() runs, verified by reading rg-wrapper.mjs:230-234 and by the observed 594-row return for a 594-match scope.
